In the mathematical theory of [[probability]], a '''Borel right process''', named after [[Émile Borel]], is a particular kind of continuous-time [[stochastic process|random process]].

Let <math>E</math> be a locally compact, separable, [[metric space]].
We denote by <math>\mathcal E</math> the [[Borel algebra|Borel subsets]] of <math>E</math>.
Let <math>\Omega</math> be the space of right continuous maps from <math>[0,\infty)</math> to <math>E</math> that have left limits in <math>E</math>,
and for each <math>t \in [0,\infty)</math>, denote by <math>X_t</math> the coordinate map at <math>t</math>; for
each <math>\omega \in \Omega </math>, <math>X_t(\omega) \in E</math> is the value of <math>\omega</math> at <math>t</math>. 
We denote the universal completion of <math>\mathcal E</math> by <math>\mathcal E^*</math>.
For each <math>t\in[0,\infty)</math>, let

: <math>
\mathcal F_t  = \sigma\left\{ X_s^{-1}(B) : s\in[0,t], B \in \mathcal E\right\},
</math>

: <math>
\mathcal F_t^*  = \sigma\left\{ X_s^{-1}(B) : s\in[0,t], B \in \mathcal E^*\right\},
</math>

and then, let

: <math>
\mathcal F_\infty  = \sigma\left\{ X_s^{-1}(B) : s\in[0,\infty), B \in \mathcal E\right\}, 
</math>

: <math>
\mathcal F_\infty^*  = \sigma\left\{ X_s^{-1}(B) : s\in[0,\infty), B \in \mathcal E^*\right\}.
</math>

For each Borel measurable function <math> f </math> on <math> E</math>, define, for each <math>x \in E</math>,

: <math>
U^\alpha f(x) = \mathbf E^x\left[ \int_0^\infty e^{-\alpha t} f(X_t)\, dt \right].
</math>

Since <math>P_tf(x) = \mathbf E^x\left[f(X_t)\right]</math> and the mapping given by <math>t \rightarrow X_t</math> is right continuous, we see that  
for any uniformly [[continuous function]] <math>f</math>, we have the mapping given by <math>t \rightarrow P_tf(x)</math> is right continuous.

Therefore, together with the [[monotone class theorem]], for any universally [[measurable function]] <math>f</math>, the mapping given by <math>(t,x) \rightarrow P_tf(x)</math>, is jointly measurable, that is, <math>\mathcal B([0,\infty))\otimes \mathcal E^* </math> measurable, and subsequently, the mapping is also <math>\left(\mathcal B([0,\infty))\otimes \mathcal E^*\right)^{\lambda\otimes \mu}</math>-measurable for all finite measures <math>\lambda</math> on <math>\mathcal B([0,\infty))</math> and <math>\mu</math> on <math>\mathcal E^*</math>.
Here, 
<math>\left(\mathcal B([0,\infty))\otimes \mathcal E^*\right)^{\lambda\otimes \mu}</math> is the completion of
<math>\mathcal B([0,\infty))\otimes \mathcal E^*</math> with respect
to the product measure <math>\lambda \otimes \mu</math>. 
Thus, for any bounded universally measurable function <math>f</math> on <math>E</math>,
the mapping <math>t\rightarrow P_tf(x)</math> is Lebesgue measurable, and hence, 
for each <math>\alpha \in [0,\infty) </math>, one can define

: <math> 
U^\alpha f(x) = \int_0^\infty e^{-\alpha t}P_tf(x) dt. 
</math>

There is enough joint measurability to check that <math>\{U^\alpha : \alpha \in (0,\infty)
\}</math> is a [[Markov chain|Markov resolvent]] on <math>(E,\mathcal E^*)</math>,
which uniquely associated with the Markovian semigroup <math>\{ P_t : t \in [0,\infty) \}</math>. 
Consequently, one may apply [[Fubini's theorem]] to see that

: <math> 
U^\alpha f(x) = \mathbf E^x\left[ \int_0^\infty e^{-\alpha t} f(X_t) dt \right]. 
</math>

The following are the defining properties of Borel right processes:<ref>{{harvnb|Sharpe|1988|loc=Sect. 20}}</ref>

*''' Hypothesis Droite 1''':

:For each probability measure <math>\mu</math> on <math>(E, \mathcal E)</math>, there exists a probability measure <math>\mathbf P^\mu</math> on <math>(\Omega, \mathcal F^*)</math> such that <math>(X_t, \mathcal F_t^*, P^\mu)</math> is a Markov process with initial measure <math>\mu</math> and transition semigroup <math>\{ P_t : t \in [0,\infty) \}</math>.

*''' Hypothesis Droite 2''':

:Let <math>f</math> be <math>\alpha</math>-excessive for the resolvent on <math>(E, \mathcal E^*)</math>. Then, for each probability measure <math>\mu</math> on <math>(E,\mathcal E)</math>, a mapping given by <math>t \rightarrow f(X_t)</math> is <math>P^\mu</math> [[almost surely]] right continuous on <math>[0,\infty)</math>.
